prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats 2024: “Fair Deal” Summary (≤500 words)

Overall vision
Fix broken systems (economy, NHS, housing, climate, politics) and restore trust, accountability and international cooperation, especially with Europe. Five themes: a stronger, greener economy; world‑class public services; a protected environment; a secure, outward‑looking UK; and a truly fair democracy.

Key pledges by area
- Economy and tax: Green-led growth via major investment in renewables, home insulation and clean industry; apprenticeships and £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants (aim £10,000); overhaul parental leave; support SMEs; replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy; repair EU trade ties; fiscal rules to cut debt share; reverse bank tax cuts; proper windfall tax on oil/gas; fairer capital gains; 4% tax on FTSE100 share buybacks; priority future income-tax cut by raising personal allowance; expand British Business Bank; national financial inclusion strategy.

- Jobs and work: Industrial strategy; R&D to 3% of GDP by 2030; Horizon Europe; clear AI rules; local banking; tackle late payments; replace apprenticeship levy with broader skills levy; modernise rights (new “dependent contractor” status, zero-hours premium, fixed-hours right); strengthen sick pay; day-one parental rights; living wage review; new Worker Protection Enforcement Authority.

- Climate and energy: Net zero by 2045; 90% renewable electricity by 2030; 10‑year home upgrade (free insulation/heat pumps for low-income); rooftop solar push; social energy tariff; decouple electricity from gas; end fossil subsidies; no fracking/new coal; invest in storage and interconnectors; empower community energy; Net Zero Delivery Authority; restore 0.7% aid with climate priority.

- NHS and care: Right to see a GP in 7 days (24h urgent), 8,000 more GPs; NHS dental access guarantee; youth mental health hubs and school professionals; cancer treatment within 62 days; public health focus; tech upgrades; independent pay review. Social care: free personal care; workforce plan; Royal College of Care Workers; Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/hour); paid carer’s leave and respite; cross‑party funding deal.

- Education and families: Per‑pupil funding above inflation; fix buildings; tutoring guarantee; early years boost and EYPP tripled; free school meals for all in poverty; restore maintenance grants; SEND funding/body; teacher pay/CPD strategy. Parental leave: double statutory maternity/shared parental pay to £350/week; 90% pay for paternity plus an extra month; day-one rights; Erasmus Plus return.

- Welfare and pensions: Scrap two‑child limit and benefit cap; target to end deep poverty in a decade; protect triple lock; fair WASPI compensation; increase and widen Carer’s Allowance; fix Universal Credit waits and sanctions.

- Crime and justice: Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance for all burglaries; Online Crime Agency; tackle court backlogs; better domestic abuse response; youth diversion; fraud reimbursement; deeper EU security cooperation.

- Nature and environment: End sewage scandal (tough new regulator, public‑benefit water firms, bonus ban, Sewage Tax); binding targets to “double nature” by 2050; 60m trees/year; Clean Air Act; boost watchdogs; deposit return; phase out non‑recyclable single‑use plastics.

- Food and farming: National Food Strategy; +£1bn/year for ELMS; high standards in trade; SPS/vet deal with EU; stronger Groceries Code Adjudicator; animal welfare bill.

- Housing: 380,000 homes/year incl. 150,000 social; garden cities; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; ban no‑fault evictions, default three‑year tenancies, landlord register; council powers to end Right to Buy; remove unsafe cladding; Rent to Own; end rough sleeping.

- Local government and transport: Multi‑year council funding; control of second homes/short lets; universal gigabit; EV shift (charging rollout, plug‑in grant, 2030 ZEV mandate); freeze rail fares; major rail electrification and Northern Powerhouse Rail; stronger buses; active travel; more road maintenance.

- Immigration and asylum: End Hostile Environment; scrap Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda plan; safe legal routes; 3‑month asylum decision standard; allow work after 3 months; flexible visa system; reverse family visa thresholds; protect EU citizens’ rights.

- Rights and democracy: Defend HRA/ECHR; ban conversion therapy; misogyny as hate crime; flexible work right; PR (STV) for MPs and English councils; scrap voter ID; votes at 16; cap donations; written federal constitution.

- Defence and international: Grow Army (aim >100k), raise defence spend towards 2.5% GDP, maintain nuclear deterrent; fix procurement; support NATO and Ukraine; restore aid to 0.7%; four‑stage plan to rebuild EU ties (ultimately seek Single Market); back two‑state solution and Gaza ceasefire; seize Russian assets; fund BBC World Service.
